stem.text:
Solve the following equation algebraically:

$  log  _(3 )\(x - 4 \)+ log  _(3 )\(x - 2 \)= 1   $

extensions.latexSource:
Solve the following equation algebraically:

\[ \log _{3}(x-4)+\log _{3}(x-2)=1 \]

solution.text:
Method 1

$   log  _(3 )\(x - 4 \)+ log  _(3 )\(x - 2 \) & = 1  \  log  _(3 )\(x - 4 \)\(x - 2 \) & = 1  \  3 ^(1 ) & = \(x - 4 \)\(x - 2 \) \  3  & = x ^(2 )- 6  x + 8  \  0  & = x ^(2 )- 6  x + 5  \  0  & = \(x - 5 \)\(x - 1 \) \  x  & = 5    $

1 mark for product rule

1 mark for exponential form

$frac(1 ,2 )$ mark for solving for $x $ within a quadratic equation

$frac(1 ,2 )$ mark for rejecting extraneous root

3 marks

Method 2

$   log  _(3 )\(x - 4 \)+ log  _(3 )\(x - 2 \) & = 1  \  log  _(3 )\(x - 4 \)\(x - 2 \) & = 1  \  log  _(3 )lr(\( x ^(2 )- 6  x + 8 \) ) & = log  _(3 ) 3  \  x ^(2 )- 6  x + 8  & = 3  \  x ^(2 )- 6  x + 5  & = 0  \  \(x - 1 \)\(x - 5 \) & = 0  \  x < 1  quad  x  & = 5    $

1 mark for product rule

$frac(1 ,2 )$ mark for logarithmic form

$frac(1 ,2 )$ mark for equating arguments

$frac(1 ,2 )$ mark for solving for $x $ within a quadratic equation

$frac(1 ,2 )$ mark for rejecting extraneous roots

3 marks
